senses.gloss:
Vaijayantī
(‘that which conquers the enemies’)
------------------------------------------
The वैजयन्ती or Vaijayanta is the name of the flower-garland adorning विष्णु’s neck. It is symbolical of the five sūkṣmabhūtas (the subtle elements). Lord विष्णु being the creator and sustainer of this world, even the subtle elements out of which he creates, are like a garland or an ornament for him.
The Kṛṣṇopaniṣad (22) mentions Vaija-yantī as representing the element wind.
The word may also indicate the flag of a king who conquers others.

vaijātya
(‘of a different nature’)
------------------------------------------
This is one of the eleven kinds of तर्क or लोगिच्. (See TARKA.)
If somebody says that, since शब्द (sound) and rūpa (form) are both indriya-grāhya (perceived by the sense-organs), let them be considered identical, the reply is that the sense-organs that perceive them (i.e., the ear and the eye) being vijāti (of different natures) they (śabda and rūpa) too are different. This kind of argument is वैजात्य.
